# Your first Harborpad sandbox

This walkthrough takes a new engineer from an accepted workspace invitation to a usable scratch environment. Have the hp CLI installed before starting. Keep the invitation nearby so that you can compare its workspace with the one you select. The examples use north-lab; use the workspace named in your own invitation when you run the commands. Workspace slugs contain only lowercase ASCII letters and hyphens.

## Sign in as yourself

Run `hp login --device` and complete the browser approval flow. The resulting token is valid for 12 hours. Use `hp session` to inspect its expiration when you return after a break. The credential belongs to your current operating-system user, so copying a project directory to a colleague does not copy your login.

There is one special route for an air-gapped training room: your sponsor can supply a one-use exchange code for `hp login --exchange CODE`. That route produces the same 12-hour token and does not add any role. Keep the code out of a support handoff, just as you would keep the resulting token out of it.

## Create an environment

Run `hp sandbox create --workspace north-lab`. Read both identifiers in the response before moving on. The workspace_id identifies the team workspace and stays stable across its sandboxes. The env_id identifies the sandbox you just created. Save the latter for commands that take ENV_ID; the workspace identifier is not a substitute for it.

Each sandbox has a 2 GiB writable quota for /work. The shared /catalog mount is read-only and does not consume that quota. If writing to /work produces a disk-full error, remove unneeded files from /work rather than trying to change /catalog.

Vendor observers follow a smaller path. That role can inspect a sandbox created by a sponsor, but cannot create one or open a shell. Ask the sponsor for its env_id and proceed to the status command. A creation failure for that role is not evidence that the invitation named the wrong workspace.

## Check the result and enter

Run `hp sandbox status ENV_ID`. The state value `ready` means that the sandbox accepts shell sessions. Check the workspace identity against the invitation as part of this first setup. The billing_project value is an accounting label for information only; seeing it does not give you billing permissions.

For the standard engineer path, use `hp shell ENV_ID` once the sandbox is ready. The endpoint of this walkthrough is a ready sandbox in the invited workspace. Vendor observers stop at inspection, because their role does not include a shell.

## Return after a break

Harborpad pauses a sandbox after 30 minutes without a sandbox API request. Merely leaving a terminal window open does not send a request and does not keep it active. A pause is therefore compatible with finding the old terminal still visible on your laptop.

Resume a paused environment with `hp sandbox start ENV_ID`; this preserves /work. The similarly named `hp sandbox recreate ENV_ID` replaces the sandbox and discards /work. Choose the operation based on whether you intend to retain that directory. An expired login does not itself discard the directory.

## Working-directory notes

Each sandbox has a 2 GiB writable quota for /work. The shared /catalog mount is read-only and does not consume that quota. If writing to /work produces a disk-full error, remove unneeded files from /work rather than trying to change /catalog.

## Authentication details for later

The normal sign-in command is `hp login --device`, which asks you to approve access in a browser. Credentials last 12 hours, and `hp session` tells you when the current one expires. This login is attached to the operating-system user running hp, rather than traveling with a copied project folder.

## Ask for help with a concrete result

Send support the workspace_id, env_id, observed state, and command that failed. These values let the recipient distinguish the workspace from the particular sandbox and see which step you reached. Do not include tokens or exchange codes. For a vendor-observer handoff, report the sponsor-provided environment identifier rather than trying the creation step to obtain a new one.
